newsitem.title: USA: FIRST ROUND SCORES FROM QUAD CITY CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: FIRST ROUND SCORES FROM QUAD CITY CLASSIC.

text.p: Gary Hallberg
birdied three of the final four holes to post a five-under-par
65 on Thursday that gave him a one-stroke lead after the
opening round of the $1.35 million Quad City Classic.
Hallberg, who had just one bogey on the day, was one shot
better than Russ Cochran, Dave Stockton Jr. and rookie Sean
McCarty, with 20 other golfers bunched together at three-under
67, two strokes off the pace.
"A 65 is an awfully good score," said Hallberg, who
finished 358th on the PGA Tour money list last year. "I've got
to be patient. I'm just going to go along for the ride."
In his only two other tour events this season, the
40-year-old Hallberg failed to break 72 and missed both cuts.
"I just had a couple of good (swing) thoughts today and it
worked well. Today, I had my brother caddie for my and I was
loose," said Hallberg, who has three career tournament wins to
his credit. "All of the good players are relaxed."
Also relaxed was Hallberg's most improbable pursuer -- the
long-hitting McCarty, who played his college golf at nearby
University of Iowa.
In his PGA Tour debut, the 24-year-old McCarty briefly
held the lead alone at five under par before finishing at 66
along with Cochran and Stockton.
Hitting drives reminiscent of another PGA Tour novice who
nearly made last year's Quad-City tournament his first
professional win -- Tiger Woods -- McCarty said he accepted a
sponsors invite to the tournament with winning on his mind.
"That way I won't have to go to qualifying school," he
said confidently.
